labs.title: Fuse ranked candidate lists
labs.instructions: Implement solve(rankings). Add 1/(60 + one-based rank) for each unique document in each ranking. Return every unique ID ordered by descending score, breaking score ties by ascending ID. Inputs contain no repeated ID within one list.
hints: Use a Map, not object-property lookups.
A document can contribute once per input ranking; use the union of IDs.

labs.title: Guard a confirmation decision
labs.instructions: Implement solve(request). Return true only when actor === owner, scopes includes "requests:confirm", and status is "pending". Assume strings and an array of scopes. This pure fixture teaches a policy check; a real server must enforce it atomically with the effect.
hints: Use the authenticated actor; never trust an owner supplied by the caller.

labs.title: Measure retrieval precision and recall
labs.instructions: Implement solve(data) returning {"precision": number, "recall": number}. data has ranking, relevant, and k. Evaluate ranking[:k]; relevant IDs form a set. Empty retrieved results give precision 0; empty relevance gives recall 0. Fixtures have unique ranked IDs and nonnegative k.
hints: Count the intersection of the returned IDs and relevant IDs.
Precision and recall use different denominators.

labs.title: Calculate stable attention weights
labs.instructions: Implement solve(data) for one query. data contains query and keys, equal nonzero vector dimensions. Compute dot(query,key)/sqrt(d), apply numerically stable softmax by subtracting the maximum score, and return weights rounded to 6 decimals. Use only the math standard-library module.
labs.solution:
import math

def solve(data):
    query, keys = data["query"], data["keys"]
    scores = [sum(a*b for a,b in zip(query,key))/math.sqrt(len(query)) for key in keys]
    largest = max(scores)
    exps = [math.exp(score-largest) for score in scores]
    total = sum(exps)
    return [round(value/total, 6) for value in exps]
hints: The attention scale uses the key/query dimension d.
exp(large) can overflow. Subtracting the maximum leaves softmax probabilities unchanged.
